title: pr-35876-add-vpc-control-plane-provisioning-terraform-aws-subnets-endpoints-sgs-peering-dns.json
author: Jordan Blake
title_short: Add VPC control plane provisioning Terraform module (subnets/endpoints/SGs/peering/DNS)
description: Add a Terraform module and accompanying Helm/installer changes to provision the Private Control Plane networking resources required for VPC-based Private deployments. This PR introduces reusable terraform resources to create private subnets, managed endpoints (VPC endpoints for SSM, ECR, S3), security groups with least-privilege rules for control-plane components, optional cross-account VPC peering for onboarding customer-managed infra, and Route53 private hosted zone records for control-plane DNS. Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private need a repeatable, audited way to provision the control plane network surface without manual console steps. The module is opinionated but configurable: it supports public/private subnet selection, multi-AZ CIDR assignment, tags, endpoint toggles, and peering accept/deny policies. Also includes Helm chart tweaks to honor the new controlPlane.hosts and nodeSelectors for private deployments and updates to the private installer docs and examples. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module for control-plane-vpc (subnets, route tables, endpoints) - [x] Security group templates and IAM role assume policy updates - [x] Cross-account peering support with optional route propagation - [x] Route53 private hosted zone and A/NS record outputs - [x] Helm chart values and templating changes to consume DNS and SG ids - [x] Docs and quickstart example (terraform + helm) - [x] Unit test plan and terratest scaffolding - [x] Manual validation in staging VPC Notes on compatibility: changes are additive and guarded by feature flags; defaults preserve existing behavior for current Private installs. See linked Linear tasks for rollout plan and gating.

review_conversation: Ava Chen (2026-02-21): Overall looks good. Two security questions: 1) are SG egress rules scoped to required control plane CIDRs only? 2) do endpoint policies restrict S3/ECR access to Redwood buckets?

Jordan Blake (2026-02-21): SGs are scoped to control-plane CIDRs in variables.tf and default to private subnets only. Endpoint policies are optional and scoped to account/bucket ARNs when enabled; updated README to call this out.
Diego Martinez (2026-02-22): Please add an explicit acceptance test for peering route propagation. Also we should document rollback steps if peering fails mid-rollout.
Jordan Blake (2026-02-23): Added terratest case to check route table entries after peering accept and added rollback script to scripts/upgrade/rollback-control-plane.sh. PTAL.
Priya Rao (2026-02-24): CI initially failed on fmt/lint and some helm templating edgecases. After fixes CI passed; approving pending a small docs clarification.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-25): Verified staging deployment end-to-end, DNS records created in private hosted zone, control plane services healthy. Approving for merge.
merge_commit_message: Add control_plane_vpc terraform module + helm and docs updates to enable Private control plane provisioning
release_notes: Added a Terraform module to provision Private Control Plane networking (subnets, endpoints, security groups, VPC peering, and Route53 private DNS). Helm chart updates allow the control plane to consume provisioned DNS and SG ids. This enables repeatable, auditable private deployments and simplifies onboarding for customer VPCs.
manual_validation: Deployed module in staging (us-east-1) with feature flags enabled. Verified: subnets created across 3 AZs, interface endpoints for SSM/ECR created, private hosted zone and A records created, peering established and route tables populated, control plane services became healthy and resolvable via private DNS.
notes_for_ops: When rolling out to customer accounts, ensure the peering acceptance policy is coordinated with the customer's network team. Use scripts/upgrade/rollback-control-plane.sh to revert peering and remove route table entries if platform components fail to register. Monitor VPC endpoint ENIs and DNS entries in Route53 for propagation delays.
security_considerations: All endpoints created are optional and default to off. Security groups follow least-privilege by default and are parameterized. IAM role changes limited to assume-role for provisioning; no broad account-wide policies introduced. Recommend a full security review before enabling cross-account peering in production.
notes: This PR is part of the Private deployment automation epic; follow-up work includes parameterizing NAT options, additional endpoint types, and adding multi-region templates.
